- 34 years of experience in agricultural produce exports, cited by management as having built trust among customers worldwide
- Robust buyer and seller network enhancing competitiveness
- In-house manufacturing and quality testing facilities supporting service continuity and product integrity
- Own consumer-facing brand 'ROHINI' for cattle feed and animal feed supplements in the domestic market
- Reputation for quality and trust among global customers; honoured with the Northern Region Export Excellence Award during the year
- Diversified product portfolio spanning cereals, spices, feed ingredients and nutritional supplements across domestic and export channels
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export concentration and dependence on overseas trade policy — Export sales contributed approximately 56% of total revenue, and management attributes the year's export shortfall directly to changes in tax policies, tariffs in other countries and ongoing war situations. Government export policies, foreign trade policies of India and importing countries, and trade restrictions are each listed by management as risks beyond the Company's control.
- Agricultural commodity price volatility — The core business is agricultural products, so management flags price fluctuations in agricultural commodities at national and global levels as an inherent and uncontrollable exposure that can significantly affect performance.
- Foreign exchange volatility — With the majority of revenue from exports, currency exchange volatility is listed under both 'Risks and Industry Challenges' and 'Risks and Concerns'. Other income depends materially on foreign exchange gains, making earnings sensitive to currency movement.
- Customer default / receivables credit risk — Management states the risk of customer defaults, both domestic and international, remains elevated given the volatile pricing environment and market liquidity concerns. The Directors' Report separately notes the Company continues to pursue legal measures for recovery of outstanding dues from defaulting debtors. Mitigation cited: stringent buyer verification protocols and trade credit insurance policies.
- Monsoon and climate dependence — Climatic conditions including monsoons and weather variability head management's list of unpredictable risks; the FY27 outlook is expressly conditioned on expectations of a favourable monsoon, and dependence on monsoon conditions is named a key factor influencing sector performance.
- Shipping and logistics disruption — Listed by management among the risks the Company is exposed to in the normal course of business — material for a business whose majority revenue moves as physical bulk agri-commodity across borders.
- Geopolitical and trade-dynamics disruption — Geopolitical developments both domestic and international are named as a risk, and management explicitly attributes part of the export decline to ongoing war situations and changing global trade dynamics.
- Legal, regulatory and fiscal-policy change — Legal and regulatory changes and changes in government trade and fiscal policies are listed among the risk spectrum; the Company operates a Risk Management Policy setting standards for assessing risks, evaluating probability and impact, and action plans for timely mitigation, with periodic reviews of operational areas.

business.body: Unique Organics Limited manufactures and exports agricultural commodities including food products, spices, herbs, ruminant feed and other animal feed supplements. Exports are driven by cereals (rice, maize, barley) and animal feed ingredients such as soybean meal/extractions, RSM and de-oiled rice bran, while the domestic business focuses on cattle feed, feed supplements and animal nutritional products sold under the 'ROHINI' brand. Operations are organised around two reportable segments, Manufacturing Activities and Trading Activities, serving buyers in India and overseas markets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Exports (cereals & feed ingredients):** Rice, Maize, Barley, Soybean Meal/Extractions, RSM (rapeseed meal), De-oiled Rice Bran, Spices, Herbs
- **Domestic animal nutrition (brand 'ROHINI'):** Cattle feed, Feed supplements, Toxin binders, Vitamin supplements, Calcium products, Binola Khal, Calf Starter, Super Transition Feed
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- 34 years of experience in agricultural produce exports, cited by management as having built trust among customers worldwide
- Robust buyer and seller network enhancing competitiveness
- In-house manufacturing and quality testing facilities supporting service continuity and product integrity
- Own consumer-facing brand 'ROHINI' for cattle feed and animal feed supplements in the domestic market
- Reputation for quality and trust among global customers; honoured with the Northern Region Export Excellence Award during the year
- Diversified product portfolio spanning cereals, spices, feed ingredients and nutritional supplements across domestic and export channels
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Rebalance the revenue mix away from trading-led income towards domestic manufacturing, which management describes as its continued focus on strengthening core business operations
- Expand the export footprint into new geographies, with a stated focus on Gulf and Middle Eastern countries and a planned entry into Sri Lanka with maize and non-basmati rice
- Broaden the product basket in animal nutrition, having launched Binola Khal, Calf Starter and Transition Feed this year, with poultry feed, toxin binders, mineral mixtures and bypass proteins intended next
- Explore export opportunities for spices in European markets
- Build the domestic ROHINI brand through product customisation, focused marketing and branding, competitive pricing, and expansion of the distribution network and digital sales platforms
- Deepen rural last-mile reach through 'Rohini Choupal' outlets across rural areas of Jaipur and participation in rural trade fairs such as Sheetla Mata Mela and Pushkar Mela, Ajmer
- Appoint new overseas agents to explore and tap emerging global markets
- Maintain financial discipline through cost optimisation measures to improve operational efficiency
- Protect receivables through stringent buyer verification protocols and trade credit insurance, and continue legal recovery action against defaulting debtors
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report contains no capex programme, project pipeline or capacity-addition narrative. Expansion is expressed entirely as market and product footprint rather than physical asset build-out: the Company launched Binola Khal, Calf Starter and Super Transition Feed during FY26, plans to introduce maize and non-basmati rice in Sri Lanka, intends to add poultry feed plus toxin binders, mineral mixtures and bypass proteins, sees export openings in maize, soybean, barley and green millets in the Gulf, and is exploring spice exports to Europe. Distribution build-out comprised new overseas agents and 'Rohini Choupal' rural outlets across rural areas of Jaipur, alongside expansion of the distribution network and digital sales platforms. The Directors' Report says only that the Company's manufacturing facilities operated efficiently during the year; no plant, line, commissioning, debottlenecking or capacity-addition project is named or dated anywhere in the bundle. Sourced from the MD&A and Directors' Report sections carried in the profile and strategy bundles of this same annual report, because the section routed into this capex bundle under the MD&A header contains no capex content (see notes).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the outlook for agricultural and allied sectors in FY 2026-27 to remain cautiously optimistic, supported by improving demand conditions, government initiatives for agriculture and exports, and expectations of a favourable monsoon
- The animal feed and agri-commodity sectors are expected to benefit from continued focus on livestock productivity, dairy development and rural demand
- The Indian animal feed market is cited (IMARC) as growing at a 6.6% CAGR from 2026-2034, framing the domestic opportunity
- Toxin binders witnessed significant demand in international markets during the year, which management highlights as a product-level demand driver
- Management anticipates good volume of business in the year ahead and remains optimistic about continued growth in both export and domestic markets
- The domestic manufacturing segment grew during the year while overall revenue moderated, which management presents as a gradual shift towards a more balanced revenue mix
- Headwinds management names for the export shortfall: changes in tax policies, exchange rate movements, tariffs in other countries and ongoing war situations
- Raw material price fluctuations, changing global trade dynamics and monsoon dependence are cited as key factors that will continue to influence sector performance

open.item: The Board recommends a dividend of Rs 1.30 per share of Rs 10 each (13%) for FY 2025-26, subject to approval of the Members at the ensuing AGM.
Introduce grains such as maize and non-basmati rice in the Sri Lankan market as part of its business expansion strategy.
Introduce poultry feed along with animal nutritional supplements such as toxin binders, mineral mixtures and bypass proteins for the livestock and poultry sectors.
Develop new export markets in Gulf and Middle Eastern countries, seeing opportunities in maize, soybean, barley and green millets.
Explore export opportunities for spices in European markets.

Management flags elevated risk of customer defaults, domestic and international, given volatile pricing and market liquidity, mitigated by stringent buyer verification protocols and trade credit insurance.
Continue diversifying beyond trading-led income streams by strengthening the domestic manufacturing base towards a more balanced revenue mix.
Strengthen domestic market presence through product customisation, focused marketing and branding, competitive pricing, and expansion of the distribution network and digital sales platforms.
Continue appointing new overseas agents to explore and tap emerging global markets as part of its growth strategy.
Maintain financial discipline through effective cost optimisation measures to support operational efficiency and long-term sustainable growth.
